properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 18 at 1:01PM CDT until September 22 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Little Rock has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Arkansas...

Cache River Near Patterson affecting Jackson and Woodruff Counties.

For the Cache River...including Patterson...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Cache River near Patterson.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Low swampy timberland along the river begins
to flood. Flood gates should be closed and equipment moved out of
the low grounds along the river and tributaries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 12:15 PM CDT Friday was 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.1 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage early
Monday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.1
feet on 07/23/2023.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

River forecasts are based on current conditions and rainfall
forecasted to occur over the next 24 hours. During periods of
flooding...Evening forecasts are reissued with updated rainfall
forecasts.

Observed and forecasted stage data plots are available on our
Advanced Hydrologic Prediction Service web page at...
www.weather.gov/lzk

Under the Current Conditions section...Select River and Lakes AHPS.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 18 at 4:13PM MDT until September 18 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Mesa County in west central Colorado...

* Until 715 PM MDT.

* At 413 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.4 and 0.8 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 3 inches in
1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Loma and Mack. This includes portions of I-70 between mile markers
8 and 15.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging currents in a matter
of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become life
threatening in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams
or creeks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 18 at 9:18AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Friday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late Saturday night.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM MDT Friday the stage was 15.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:00 PM MDT Friday was 15.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.5 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
early tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 800 AM MDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM THIS AFTERNOON TO LATE SATURDAY NIGHT
